key_insight: Biologically inspired e-prop training matched backpropagation through time at 100% survival, while more biologically faithful learning schemes performed substantially worse.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest biologically inspired spiking controllers can support humanoid locomotion, but stronger biological fidelity can limit control performance.
method: Distill a reinforcement learning expert into a spiking network using dataset aggregation.
Compare frozen recurrent weights, reward-modulated STDP, e-prop, and backpropagation through time.
Evaluate locomotion survival and demonstrate brief stepping on the Unitree H1-2 humanoid.
evidence_signal: Reported survival rates were 100% for e-prop and backpropagation through time, approximately 43.7% for the fixed reservoir, and approximately 11% for reward-modulated STDP.
watch_item: Brief hardware stepping does not establish sustained real-world locomotion robustness or successful control by a living neural culture.
paper_title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
